audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for plot, Bethany anointing, Judas, Passover meal, covenant blood, Gethsemane, arrest, young man fleeing, trial, Son of Humanity saying, and Peter denial.

verses.restored: Now the Passover and Unleavened Bread were after two days. The chief priests and scribes were seeking how, by deceit, they might seize him and kill him.

familiar.text: After two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.

verses.restored: For they were saying, Not during the feast, lest there be an uproar of the people.

familiar.text: But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar of the people.

verses.restored: While he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very costly pure nard ointment. Breaking the jar, she poured it over his head.

familiar.text: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.

verses.restored: Some were indignant among themselves: Why has this ointment been wasted?

familiar.text: And there were some that had indignation within themselves, and said, Why was this waste of the ointment made?

verses.restored: For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor. And they were scolding her.

familiar.text: For it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and have been given to the poor. And they murmured against her.

verses.restored: But Jesus said, Leave her. Why do you trouble her? She has worked a beautiful/good work in me.

familiar.text: And Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.

verses.restored: For the poor you always have with you, and whenever you wish you are able to do good for them; but me you do not always have.

familiar.text: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.

verses.restored: What she had, she did. She anointed my body beforehand for burial.

familiar.text: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: wherever the good message is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken in memory of her.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

verses.restored: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests so that he might hand him over to them.

familiar.text: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went unto the chief priests, to betray him unto them.

verses.restored: Hearing this, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver. And he sought how he might hand him over at a good time.

familiar.text: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.

verses.restored: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples said to him, Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?

familiar.text: And the first day of unleavened bread, when they killed the passover, his disciples said unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and prepare that thou mayest eat the passover?

verses.restored: He sends two of his disciples and says to them, Go into the city, and a person carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him.

familiar.text: And he sendeth forth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go ye into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.

verses.restored: Wherever he enters, say to the house-master, The Teacher says, Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?

familiar.text: And wheresoever he shall go in, say ye to the goodman of the house, The Master saith, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

verses.restored: He will show you a large upper room furnished and ready; prepare there for us.

familiar.text: And he will shew you a large upper room furnished and prepared: there make ready for us.

verses.restored: The disciples went out, came into the city, and found it just as he said to them; and they prepared the Passover.

familiar.text: And his disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.

verses.restored: When evening came, he came with the twelve.

familiar.text: And in the evening he cometh with the twelve.

verses.restored: As they reclined and ate, Jesus said, Amen, I say to you: one of you will hand me over, one eating with me.

familiar.text: And as they sat and did eat, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you which eateth with me shall betray me.

verses.restored: They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one, Surely not I?

familiar.text: And they began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him one by one, Is it I? and another said, Is it I?

verses.restored: He said to them, One of the twelve, the one dipping with me into the bowl.

familiar.text: And he answered and said unto them, It is one of the twelve, that dippeth with me in the dish.

verses.restored: For the Son of Humanity goes as it has been written about him, but woe to that person through whom the Son of Humanity is handed over; beautiful/good for that person if he had not been born.

familiar.text: The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had never been born.

verses.restored: As they were eating, taking bread, blessing, he broke it, gave it to them, and said, Take; this is my body.

familiar.text: And as they did eat, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and brake it, and gave to them, and said, Take, eat: this is my body.

verses.restored: Taking a cup, giving thanks, he gave it to them, and they all drank from it.

familiar.text: And he took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave it to them: and they all drank of it.

verses.restored: He said to them, This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: I will certainly not drink again of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, I will drink no more of the fruit of the vine, until that day that I drink it new in the kingdom of God.

verses.restored: After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

familiar.text: And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, You will all stumble, for it has been written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.

familiar.text: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.

verses.restored: But after I am raised, I will go before you to Galilee.

familiar.text: But after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.

verses.restored: Peter said to him, Even if all stumble, yet not I.

familiar.text: But Peter said unto him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Amen, I say to you: today, this night, before a rooster sounds twice, you will deny me three times.

familiar.text: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this day, even in this night, before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.

verses.restored: But he spoke emphatically, If I must die with you, I will certainly not deny you. All said likewise.

familiar.text: But he spake the more vehemently, If I should die with thee, I will not deny thee in any wise. Likewise also said they all.

verses.restored: They came to a place named Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, Sit here while I pray.

familiar.text: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith to his disciples, Sit ye here, while I shall pray.

verses.restored: He takes Peter, James, and John with him, and began to be deeply distressed and troubled.

familiar.text: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be sore amazed, and to be very heavy;

verses.restored: He said to them, My soul/life is deeply grieved to the point of death; remain here and keep watch.

familiar.text: And saith unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death: tarry ye here, and watch.

verses.restored: Going forward a little, he fell on the ground and prayed that, if possible, the hour might pass from him.

familiar.text: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.

verses.restored: He said, Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; take this cup away from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will.

familiar.text: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.

verses.restored: He comes and finds them sleeping, and says to Peter, Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not strong enough to keep watch one hour?

familiar.text: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest not thou watch one hour?

verses.restored: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.

familiar.text: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.

verses.restored: Again he went away and prayed, saying the same word.

familiar.text: And again he went away, and prayed, and spake the same words.

verses.restored: Again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy; and they did not know what to answer him.

familiar.text: And when he returned, he found them asleep again, (for their eyes were heavy,) neither wist they what to answer him.

verses.restored: He comes the third time and says to them, Sleep the rest and rest? It is enough. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Humanity is handed over into the hands of sinners/misaligned ones.

familiar.text: And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

verses.restored: Rise, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has drawn near.

familiar.text: Rise up, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand.

verses.restored: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.

familiar.text: And immediately, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

verses.restored: The one handing him over had given them a sign, saying, Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him and lead him away securely.

familiar.text: And he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.

verses.restored: Coming, immediately he approached him and said, Rabbi, and kissed him.

familiar.text: And as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him.

verses.restored: They laid hands on him and seized him.

familiar.text: And they laid their hands on him, and took him.

verses.restored: One of those standing by drew a sword, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

familiar.text: And one of them that stood by drew a sword, and smote a servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs to arrest me?

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staves to take me?

verses.restored: Day by day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me; but let the Scriptures be fulfilled.

familiar.text: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.

verses.restored: Leaving him, all fled.

familiar.text: And they all forsook him, and fled.

verses.restored: A certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body; they seized him.

familiar.text: And there followed him a certain young man, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body; and the young men laid hold on him:

verses.restored: But he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.

familiar.text: And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.

verses.restored: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes gathered.

familiar.text: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and with him were assembled all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.

verses.restored: Peter followed him from far away, right into the courtyard of the high priest, and was sitting with the attendants, warming himself at the fire.

familiar.text: And Peter followed him afar off, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.

verses.restored: The chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus to put him to death, but they were not finding any.

familiar.text: And the chief priests and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.

verses.restored: For many were bearing false witness against him, and their testimonies were not equal.

familiar.text: For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together.

verses.restored: Some stood and bore false witness against him, saying,

familiar.text: And there arose certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,

verses.restored: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple made with hands, and through three days I will build another not made with hands.

familiar.text: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.

verses.restored: Even so their testimony was not equal.

familiar.text: But neither so did their witness agree together.

verses.restored: The high priest stood in the middle and questioned Jesus, saying, Do you answer nothing? What are these testifying against you?

familiar.text: And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?

verses.restored: But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest questioned him and said, Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed?

familiar.text: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said unto him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?

verses.restored: Jesus said, I am; and you will see the Son of Humanity sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.

familiar.text: And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

verses.restored: The high priest tore his garments and said, What further need do we have of witnesses?

familiar.text: Then the high priest rent his clothes, and saith, What need we any further witnesses?

verses.restored: You heard the blasphemy. What appears to you? They all condemned him as liable to death.

familiar.text: Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.

verses.restored: Some began to spit on him, cover his face, strike him, and say to him, Prophesy. The attendants received him with slaps.

familiar.text: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesy: and the servants did strike him with the palms of their hands.

verses.restored: As Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest's servant girls came.

familiar.text: And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:

verses.restored: Seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus.

familiar.text: And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.restored: But he denied it, saying, I neither know nor understand what you mean. He went out into the forecourt, and a rooster sounded.

familiar.text: But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.

verses.restored: The servant girl, seeing him, began again to say to those standing by, This one is from them.

familiar.text: And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.

verses.restored: Again he denied it. After a little while, those standing by again said to Peter, Truly you are from them, for you are Galilean.

familiar.text: And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilaean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.

verses.restored: But he began to curse and swear, I do not know this person you speak of.

familiar.text: But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.

verses.restored: Immediately a rooster sounded a second time. Peter remembered the word Jesus had said to him: Before a rooster sounds twice, you will deny me three times. Breaking down, he wept.

familiar.text: And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
